chunks: My father and a group narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from a man who said:

Abul Ḥasan (Imam Riďā (a.s.)) sent me some clothes that were wrapped up, in the middle of which there was some clay. I asked the person who had brought the clothes about this clay. He said, “It is the clay of the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.). He (Imam Riďā (a.s.)) does not send clothes or anything else to anyone without putting some of this clay within it and he says, ‘It is protection with the permission of Allāh.”

key_terms.طِينُ قَبْرِ الْحُسَيْنِ: Clay from the grave of Imam al-Husain

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the clay from the grave of Imam al-Husain (a.s.) in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the spiritual significance of the clay from Imam al-Ḥusain’s grave as a tangible medium of divine protection (aman), a practice consistently maintained by Imam al-Riďa (a.s.) when sending gifts. It underscores the Shia belief in the barakah (blessing) of the Ahl al-Bayt’s physical remains, linking the martyrdom of al-Ḥusain to ongoing spiritual safeguarding for the faithful.

He (Imam Riďā (a.s.)) does not send clothes or anything else to anyone without putting some of this clay within it and he says, ‘It is protection with the permission of Allāh.”
